To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) to screening mammography does not significantly reduce interval cancer rates, does not reduce recall rates and does not reduce the number of false-positive findings.

The use of computer aided detection (CAD) with screening mammography is associated with a statistically significant increase in the recall rate, the biopsy rate and the detection rate for invasive cancer, but not for DCIS.
the use of CAD for screening mammography is associated with a statistically significant decrease in cancer detection and a small but statistically significant increase in the recall rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the single reading with computer- aided detection (CAD) as a screening tool for the early detection of breast cancer.
the development of computer aided detection (CAD) systems for mammography, and with the evaluation of these systems.
the development of an automated system for the detection and diagnosis of breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
computer-aided mammography is not ready for widespread use as a screening tool.

computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems have the potential to improve the accuracy of breast cancer screening, especially in cases of difficult interpretation, such as dense breasts, and in the hands of inexperienced radiologists.
computer-aided diagnosis is not yet ready for widespread use in screening and diagnostic mammography.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that a computer aided detection (CAD) system improved cancer detection in a single reading environment.
the use of CAD for screening mammography has not been proven effective and should be discontinued.
computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) is a useful adjunct to single reading in the context of screening mammography.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of CAD in a screening program does not result in a statistically significant increase in the recall rate or the cancer detection rate.
we have developed an AI system that can detect breast cancer with a high degree of accuracy.

the use of CAD in screening mammography is a cost-effective strategy that can be implemented with minimal additional costs to the health-care system, and it can improve the detection of invasive breast cancers.
